text: Retry only on transient failures: connection errors, timeouts, and HTTP 429/502/503/504. Never retry on 4xx other than 429, and never retry on 501.
reason: These are the statuses where a second attempt has a real chance of succeeding without masking a client bug. Retrying 400/401/403/404 just delays surfacing a real error to the caller.
rejected: Retrying all 5xx uniformly (500 often indicates a deterministic server bug and 501 will never succeed on retry).

text: Use exponential backoff with full jitter: delay = random(0, min(cap, base * 2**attempt)), with base=0.5s, cap=30s, max 3 retries by default.
reason: Full jitter (per the AWS Architecture Blog analysis) spreads retry storms better than fixed or equal-jitter backoff and keeps total worst-case wait bounded. Three retries covers most transient blips without multiplying load on a struggling server by more than ~4x.
rejected: Fixed-interval retries (thundering-herd risk when many clients fail at the same moment).

text: Should retries be bounded by an overall deadline (total elapsed time) in addition to a max attempt count?
reason: A per-request timeout of 30s with 3 retries can mean a 2-minute wall-clock wait, which may violate caller expectations. A total-deadline budget is more predictable but adds API surface and interacts awkwardly with Retry-After.
